gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-vithk: Industrial, glowing-tube lines with no give. Existence does its best work in uniform, tube-like strokes and wide porthole counters, while Noto Serif Vithkuqi does its best with big round bowls and gentle thick-thin shifts.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Strong, tall letters crowd together in Franchise, drawn like outlines in a single width. And where Franchise excels at bold display lines, Noto Serif Dogra excels at curves whose thinnest points keep real weight.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-gujar: Franchise packs tall small letters into a narrow ascender strip, with no stress anywhere in its curves. Yet the strongest pull is contrast: Noto Serif Gujarati's oversized counters and moderate thick-thin shift soften Franchise's stress-free curves.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-khojk: Franchise crams tall small letters tightly together, its crossbars matching its stems in weight and its c tips pulled apart. Franchise punches; Noto Serif Khojki, with its slight pinches, whispers.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-malay: Clean, strong and crowded, Franchise draws every curve without a pinch. Noto Serif Malayalam then adds big open counters and gently thinning bowls, so the flat, uniform heading hands off to a softer, modulated text.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Strong and tightly packed, Franchise gives its joins the same weight as its strokes. Noto Serif Oriya meets it with heavier curves and a restrained thick-thin rhythm, so one stays blunt while the other settles into quiet authority.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-ottom: Drawn like a plotter pen's line, one width throughout, Franchise crowds tall small letters tight together. Franchise thrives big and brief; Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq adds mild, never stark contrast.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-telug: Franchise lays down strokes like twine pressed flat, with tall small letters jammed against their neighbors. Noto Serif Telugu, traditional and refined, moves down a page gently, its mid-range stroke gap and lowercase rising nearly to the capitals.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-thai: Strong and clean, Franchise keeps arms and legs a constant width while its tall small letters crowd shoulder to shoulder. Noto Serif Thai then reads mellow and bookish, bodies filling the line.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-tibet: Authoritative from the first line, Franchise pulls every stroke taut like a drawn string. Noto Serif Tibetan settles in with stems barely outweighing hairlines, so a full page glides along without a snag.
